primary_diagnosis_treated: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (overt) with co‑existing essential hypertension

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any change in renal function
medications.purpose: Control essential hypertension and provide renal protection
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension; NG203 recommends ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria

medications.dose: 500 mg PO once daily with evening main meal (titrate by 500 mg weekly to max 2 g/day)
medications.duration: Start 500 mg daily, titrate to target dose over 4‑6 weeks, then lifelong — review annually
medications.purpose: First‑line glucose‑lowering therapy for type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NG28 (2024 update) recommends Metformin MR + SGLT2‑i as first‑line for all T2DM

medications.dose: 10 mg PO once daily in the morning
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any change in eGFR
medications.purpose: Improve glycaemic control, reduce cardiovascular and renal risk
medications.nice_justification: NG28 (2024 update) recommends adding an SGLT2‑i at diagnosis when eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: 20 mg PO once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.nice_justification: CG181/NICE recommends statin for adults ≥40 y with QRISK ≥10 % or multiple risk factors

medications.duration: If added, lifelong — review BP after 4 weeks and adjust as needed
medications.purpose: Additional antihypertensive if target <140/80 mmHg not achieved on lisinopril alone
medications.nice_justification: NG136 recommends CCB as second‑line agent when BP remains uncontrolled

interactions_checked.interaction: Both can affect renal function; risk of lactic acidosis if eGFR falls <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
interactions_checked.action: Check eGFR before initiating Metformin and repeat at 3 months; hold Metformin if eGFR <30

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive risk of volume depletion and hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Counsel on adequate hydration; monitor BP and renal function after 1‑2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect; may increase risk of peripheral edema
interactions_checked.action: Start amlodipine at low dose, monitor BP and edema; consider dose adjustment of lisinopril if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR unknown; contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (risk of lactic acidosis)
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR <30, use SGLT2‑i alone or DPP‑4 inhibitor

contraindications.reason: eGFR unknown; SGLT2‑i requires eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² for initiation
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR 20‑29, use dapagliflozin 10 mg (per NG28) or a DPP‑4 inhibitor

contraindications.reason: None identified; listed for completeness if added

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² for initiation of Metformin and SGLT2‑i; must be measured before starting.
QRISK score not calculated – assumed ≥10 % based on age, hypertension, prediabetes, and anemia; lipid profile required to confirm statin need.
Serum potassium and electrolytes not available – baseline needed before and after ACE‑I dose changes.
Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio (ACR) not available – required for CKD staging and BP target determination.
Cause of chronic anemia not established – further work‑up (iron studies, renal anaemia screen) needed before specific therapy.
No record of recurrent genital/urinary infections – assess before SGLT2‑i initiation.
treatment_summary: Start Metformin MR 500 mg daily and empagliflozin 10 mg daily as first‑line dual therapy for newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, after confirming eGFR ≥30. Continue lisinopril 20 mg for hypertension and add amlodipine 5 mg if BP remains >140/80 mmHg after 4 weeks. Initiate atorvastatin 20 mg for primary cardiovascular prevention. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, BP, HbA1c, and lipids per NICE NG28/NG136 recommendations, and address lifestyle factors through structured education and weight‑loss programs.
